subject: Post-call recap & next steps: Atlas Health private deployment economics
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@atlashealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 13:03:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — token volumes + private deployment questions

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo and for walking through Redwood's private/VPC option this morning. As promised, attaching a quick token-volume export and rough monthly profile so you can sketch pricing back-of-envelope. Key items from our side: 

- Estimated baseline traffic: ~50M tokens/month for core user flows (Q1).
- Peak testing and training windows: up to ~220M tokens/month during month-end experiments.
- API pattern: bursty with short-latency needs (p95 generation latency target ~250ms).
- Security: must be VPC-hosted; customer-managed key preferred.

Open questions we need answered to move to procurement:
1) How does Redwood price private deployments — is it (a) per-environment subscription + usage, (b) per-GPU reserved slab, or (c) committed token bundles with a flat support fee?
2) If we commit to an annual token volume, what is a reasonable $/1M tokens target for a three-environment setup (prod/preprod/dev)?
3) Support tiers: what do SLAs/response times look like for Gold vs Platinum for private installs?

Budget window: org has sign-off flexibility in the $75k–$200k ARR range for infra + support for year one if the unit economics work.

Next steps from our side: I can loop in procurement (procurement@atlashealth.com) once we have a model to evaluate. Please call out any must-haves that drive premium pricing.

Attachment: Atlas_Token_Sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Samantha
Head of AI Products | Atlas Health
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@atlashealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — token volumes + private deployment questions

Samantha —

Appreciate the detail and the token export, that helps a lot. Quick recap and answers so we can get you a clean proposal: 

Recap of what I heard: 
- Baseline ~50M tokens/mo, spikes to ~220M during tests.
- VPC-hosted required; customer KMS preferred.
- Need low-latency for interactive flows.

How we typically price private/VPC deployments (high-level options):
1) Environment subscription + usage overlay (common for customers with multi-envs): fixed monthly fee per private environment (covers runtime, orchestration, and per-env isolation) + usage-based token charge.
2) Committed token bundles + platform fee: customer commits to N tokens/year; we price committed tokens at a discounted unit rate and add a platform license that covers private control plane and deployment automation.
3) Dedicated reserved capacity (GPU slabs) for high predictable throughput: monthly reserved capacity priced by GPU-equivalent slab + nominal token fee for overage.

Preliminary unit-econ guidance (illustrative):
- Environment subscription: $2,500/month per environment (prod = 1x, preprod = 0.5x discount, dev = 0.3x discount negotiable).
- Committed token example: 120M tokens/month committed (1.44B/year) -> target $/1M tokens = $650–$900 depending on term and support.
- Smaller commit (25–50M/mo): target $/1M tokens = $1,200–$1,600 unless bundled with a higher platform fee.

Given your budget window ($75k–$200k ARR), a structured path we often propose: start year-one with a modest committed bundle that covers baseline (50M/mo) + environment subscription for 3 envs, with a short-term overage arrangement for spikes. That would land you in the lower-to-mid end of your budget range depending on commit size and support tier.

A few clarifying Qs so our pricing team can model concrete numbers: 
- Confirm exact environment count (prod/preprod/dev) — do you require an additional training sandbox?
- Expected concurrent request / QPS target for prod (ballpark).
- Any hard SLA requirements beyond standard Platinum (e.g., four-hour incident response, 99.9% uptime)?

I will ask Marissa to drop our support tier doc and an example quote template. If you can confirm the three/four envs and typical QPS, we can deliver a tailored proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: samantha@atlashealth.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 19:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — token volumes + private deployment questions

Hi all —

Attaching the support tier matrix and a short explainer for how environment subscriptions map to our private product. High-level differences:
- Gold: Standard business hours support, 24-hour response for P1, weekly operational reviews.
- Platinum: 24x7 on-call, 4-hour P1 response, quarterly on-site (or remote) architecture reviews, prioritized escalation path.
- Enterprise (custom): Dedicated TAM, faster SLAs, and extended retention/forensics options.

Notes on env sizing: for a 3-environment setup (prod/preprod/dev) we typically recommend:
- Prod: dedicated pool with reserve burst (handles p95 latency goal)
- Preprod: smaller reserved pool or shared dev slab with isolated control plane
- Dev: cost-optimized, can be single shared node with lower guarantee

Attachment: Redwood_Support_Tiers.pdf (pdf)

If Atlas wants lowest unit cost and predictable billing, Marissa recommends an annual committed token bundle sized at baseline * 12 with a 20–30% buffer for spikes; combine that with Platinum if low-response SLAs are required.

I'm happy to draft two quick options (Option A: 12-month commit sized to baseline; Option B: smaller commit + reserved GPU slab for spikes) and send numbers. Vivek — want me to prepare those and include the sample DocuSign/term sheet?

- Marissa
Principal Solutions | Redwood Inference

Vivek / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick answers and the support tier doc — helpful. To confirm from our side:
- Env count: 3 (prod, preprod, dev). We will also plan short-term training experiments but those will be scheduled into existing prod/preprod windows; we do not need an extra permanently-separate training environment at contract start.
- QPS: baseline concurrency is low (~8–12 concurrent requests typical), burst to ~60 concurrent during tests.
- SLA: Platinum preferred given clinical workloads; 4-hour P1 response is important.
- Budget check: procurement expects an internal target of ~$120k ARR if the unit economics and SLAs line up.

Next steps: please send Option A/B as two line-item quotes (annual pricing) and a short-term spike policy (how overages are billed). Procurement will review and route for approval if numbers align. Also include the DocuSign link and a sample SOW for private deployments so we can speed sign-off.

I'll forward this to procurement now.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of AI Products | Atlas Health
